metadata.source: Citigroup 10-K filings, commercial banking reports, FDIC branch data 2024-2025
metadata.notes: Citi has a concentrated US footprint (648 branches in 13 states) focused on major financial centers. Post-2021 consumer banking restructuring, commercial bank serves ~14K clients with strong international capabilities. Client base skews toward larger SMBs ($5M-$25M revenue) with cross-border needs.

industrySegments.name: Technology
industrySegments.description: Digital, technology, and communications companies. Strong presence in SF Bay Area and NYC tech hubs.
industrySegments.notes: Citi's strongest SMB vertical. Concentrated in SF Bay Area (40%), NYC (35%), Seattle (15%). Higher credit limits reflect international payment flows and working capital needs for cross-border operations.

industrySegments.name: Professional Services
industrySegments.description: Legal, accounting, consulting, financial advisory firms. High concentration in major metros.
industrySegments.notes: Second-largest segment. NYC dominates (50%), followed by DC (20%), Chicago (15%). Includes law firms, consulting firms, accounting practices. Strong credit profile, stable cash flows.

industrySegments.name: Healthcare & Life Sciences
industrySegments.description: Medical practices, clinics, biotech, medical device distributors, health services.
industrySegments.notes: Strong in SF (biotech/medical devices), NYC (healthcare services), Miami (medical tourism/imports). Higher utilization reflects equipment financing and inventory for distributors.

industrySegments.name: Retail & E-Commerce
industrySegments.description: Specialty retail, e-commerce, import/export retail, luxury goods.
industrySegments.notes: Largest segment by client count. Heavy e-commerce/import focus (45% have international trade). NYC (25%), LA (22%), Miami (18%), SF (12%). Trade finance is key differentiator.

industrySegments.name: Manufacturing & Distribution
industrySegments.description: Light manufacturing, importers, distributors with international supply chains.
industrySegments.notes: Highest avg credit limits due to working capital for inventory/receivables. 56% have international supply chains. LA/Long Beach port access (30%), Chicago (25%), NYC (20%).

industrySegments.name: Real Estate & Property Services
industrySegments.description: Commercial real estate, property management, REITs, development firms.
industrySegments.notes: Highest avg credit limits reflect property/project financing. NYC (40%), Miami (20%), SF (15%), LA (12%). Mix of commercial landlords, property managers, small developers.

industrySegments.name: Food Service & Hospitality
industrySegments.description: Restaurants, hotels, catering, specialty food importers in metro areas.
industrySegments.notes: Smallest segment for Citi - not a strategic focus. Concentrated in tourist/business hubs: Miami (28%), NYC (26%), SF (18%), Chicago (14%). Higher default rate typical for sector.

industrySegments.name: Other Industries
industrySegments.description: Transportation, construction, agriculture, utilities, services not elsewhere classified.
industrySegments.notes: Catch-all for industries outside core focus. Includes logistics (especially international freight), professional services not in main category, specialized B2B services.

geographicDistribution.name: Northeast
geographicDistribution.notes: Dominant region. NYC metro alone represents ~35% of total US clients. Strong in professional services (law, finance, consulting), tech (fintech/adtech), healthcare. DC presence serves government contractors and policy/lobbying firms.

geographicDistribution.name: West
geographicDistribution.notes: Second-largest region. SF Bay Area is tech/biotech hub (40% of West region clients). LA serves entertainment, import/retail, manufacturing. Strong trade finance presence at LA/Long Beach port. Seattle tech corridor growing.

geographicDistribution.name: Southeast
geographicDistribution.notes: Miami is critical international gateway (Latin America). Strong in trade finance, import/export, healthcare (medical tourism), hospitality. Limited branch presence outside Miami metro. Atlanta serves as Southeast commercial hub.

geographicDistribution.name: Midwest
geographicDistribution.notes: Almost entirely Chicago metro (90%). Serves financial services, professional services, manufacturing with international supply chains. Limited presence outside Chicago - no retail branches in other Midwest cities.

geographicDistribution.name: Southwest
geographicDistribution.notes: Minimal branch presence - mostly commercial/private banking relationships in Dallas and Houston. Serves energy sector suppliers, professional services, some tech (Austin area). Not a strategic retail banking market for Citi.

creditProfile.notes: Higher credit limits and lower default rates than industry average reflect Citi's focus on larger SMBs ($5M+ revenue) with established operations and international business. Stronger underwriting criteria and relationship banking model.

strengths: Global network and international banking capabilities
Trade finance and supply chain solutions
Strong presence in top-tier metros (NYC, SF, Miami)
Digital banking and treasury management platforms
weaknesses: Limited geographic coverage (only 13 states with branches)
Smaller overall SMB client base vs Chase/Wells/BofA
Less competitive in traditional Main Street banking
Higher minimum relationship sizes ($3M+ revenue typically)
